result_text:
The `all_files.zip` export now looks up and names its entries from the configured aspect names, so a renamed aspect no longer breaks it or `git-history.zip`. The new tests pass (2/2).

**The fix** is in `reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`, in `aspectFileLists`. It had hard-coded `aspect_*.txt` literals, so a renamed aspect made the read of the loose file fail. The method now takes the five configured aspects (`getMain()`, `getTest()`, `getGenerated()`, `getBuildAndDeployment()`, `getOther()`) and names each entry with `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`, the same call that writes the loose files. Order is unchanged, and the default configuration produces the same names as before. I also updated its Javadoc to match.

**The test** is a new `reports/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporterTest.java`. It covers the default names and the renamed `buildAndDeployment` case, which yields `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt` in fourth place.

I ran `mvn -o -pl reports test -Dtest=DataExporterTest`. I did not run an end-to-end export, so `git-history.zip` is not checked directly. It sits in the same try block, so it is written once `all_files.zip` no longer throws. Nothing is committed.
